title: Introduce jurisdictional residency shadow-mode, audit enricher, and KMS provenance validator
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation and context: Customers have asked for a non-enforcing (shadow) residency policy mode to validate policy changes and collect telemetry before a hard rollout. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a residency shadow-mode controller that evaluates per-request residency policies (geozone claims, tenant pins) but does not block traffic; 2) an audit enricher that attaches provenance metadata and normalized residency assertions to existing audit events; 3) a KMS provenance validator which separately verifies that the KMS usage recorded in the request path matches tenant-declared region constraints and emits structured evidence into audit logs. The design intentionally minimizes runtime penalty for the success path by deferring heavy verification to asynchronous workers and sampling failures for immediate alerting. Changes: - residency controller: new package internal/policy/residency_shadow with evaluator and policy cache; runs in read-only mode and writes evaluated assertions to an in-memory ring buffer and to the audit enrichment pipeline. - audit enricher: added audit/enricher service that consumes events, normalizes claim sets and attaches "residency.proof" fields; supports enrichment schemas v1 and v1.1. - kms validator: introduced kms/provenance/validator that performs deterministic checks against KMS metadata (location tags, atlas mapping) and outputs a signed assertion blob attached to the audit event when validation is successful. - routing: minor router changes to attach a residency-eval header when shadow mode is enabled for a tenant. - CLI and config: console flags to enable per-tenant shadow-mode, sampling rate, and a temporary retention window for enriched audit payloads. - tests: end-to-end integration tests in test/e2e/residency_shadow_test.go, unit coverage for policy compiler and enricher serializers. - docs: added security/residency-shadow-mode.md with rollout guidance and an FAQ for ops. Backwards compatibility & safety: Shadow-mode is opt-in per-tenant and off by default. No enforcement path was touched; the existing enforcement code path remains the source of truth. KMS validator runs asynchronously and will not fail requests. Feature flags: RESIDENCY_SHADOW_ENABLE (boolean), RESIDENCY_ENRICH_SAMPLING (float 0..1), KMS_PROV_ASYNC (boolean). Checklist: - [x] Implement residency evaluator and cache - [x] Audit enricher and schema v1.1 - [x] KMS provenance validator and offline signer - [x] Unit tests for policy compiler and serializer - [x] Integration tests for end-to-end enrichment - [x] Console flags + documentation - [x] Add telemetry counters and SLO guardrails Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to Canary with residency shadow disabled globally; enable for internal tenants at 10% sampling 2) Monitor the residency.enriched_events and kms.prov_success_rate dashboards for 48h 3) Increase sampling to 50% for pilot customers and collect false-positive/false-negative signals 4) If stable after 2 weeks, consider converting to a canary-enforce mode (separate PR). Observability and alerts: - New metrics: residency.eval_latency_ms, residency.enriched_count, kms.prov_success_rate, kms.prov_latency_ms - Alert: kms.prov_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m (P1) - Logs: structured audit events include residency.proof.v1 and kms.provenance.signature Notes on security: The KMS provenance validator verifies tag claims only; it does not access plaintext keys. Signed assertions use the internal audit-signing key and are recorded as immutable audit fields. Related work: this complements ENG-4391 (policy transfer tool) and supersedes part of ENG-4478 proposal to add an audit "residency" tag. Impact: lowers risk of sweeping enforcement rollouts by enabling high-fidelity telemetry and signed provenance evidence for compliance review.

f3b2e7a: implement audit enricher pipeline and schema migration support

review_comments: Luca Ortega: Could we avoid creating a new long-lived in-memory buffer? Suggest we use bounded channel with backpressure to avoid OOM in high throughput tenants.
Maya Chen (author): Switched ring buffer to a size-bounded channel with passive drop and added per-tenant backpressure metrics (residency.buffer_drops).
Priya Singh: Add a unit test that simulates KMS metadata mismatch and confirm the validator emits an audit.prov_mismatch counter.
Maya Chen (author): Added kms.prov_mismatch_counter unit test and an integration scenario that runs validator in async mode.
Daniel Park: The schema migration needs a compatibility note. Please document how older consumers should handle missing residency.proof.v1.1 fields.
Maya Chen (author): Added backward compatibility section to docs and a feature toggle to disable enrichment for consumers that can't handle the new fields.
release_notes: Add residency shadow evaluation (opt-in), audit enrichment with signed KMS provenance assertions, and console controls for sampling and retention. No enforcement changes. Intended for staged rollout to validate policy changes and generate compliance evidence.
